children: said Chief Operating Officer Kevin Rayment will become president and chief executive officer on Jan. 1, succeeding Lynn Bamford as part of a planned leadership transition.
Bamford, who has served as CEO for six years, will retire from the position and become executive chair. Rayment will also join Curtiss-Wright’s board.
Rayment has been COO since 2021 and has 35 years of experience across the aerospace and defense, commercial nuclear and industrial markets. He joined Curtiss-Wright
in 2004 and previously led the company’s former Commercial/Industrial segment, where his responsibilities included operations, product development, financial performance and acquisition integration.
The Davidson, North Carolina-based company said the appointment follows a planned succession process and is intended to provide continuity in its growth strategy.
Bamford has spent 22 years at Curtiss-Wright
and helped reshape the company’s portfolio during her tenure as CEO, with an increased emphasis on aerospace and defense and other higher-growth markets.

said it has generated record sales, profitability, orders, backlog and free cash flow during Bamford’s tenure. The company also returned $1.7 billion to shareholders through dividends and stock buybacks while completing several acquisitions.
Rayment said he plans to continue the company’s focus on profitable growth, margin expansion, investment and shareholder returns.
Curtiss-Wright provides engineered products and services to aerospace and defense, nuclear and industrial customers.

title: Curtiss-Wright names Kevin Rayment CEO as Lynn Bamford plans retirement
